title: The Doctor Who Told Everyone to Wash Their Hands

sections.name: The Doctor Who Told Everyone to Wash Their Hands
lines: In 1840s Vienna, women giving birth in hospital were dying of a deadly fever.
A young doctor, Ignaz Semmelweis, noticed something. Doctors were coming straight from autopsies to deliver babies.
In 1847, he made them wash their hands in chlorinated lime first.
Deaths on his ward dropped dramatically.
But many doctors were offended by the idea that their own hands were spreading disease.
Semmelweis died in 1865, mostly ignored. Today he's called the saviour of mothers.
